text:
Priya: FYI ran into a nasty edge during the overnight scale-down — some GPU spot nodes started terminating while kubelet was still streaming tokens to clients. we lost several long-running inference pods mid-request :grimacing:
Sam: ugh. do you have the termination trace? was it the cloud termination notice or an autoscaler eviction?
Priya: autoscaler triggered scale-down on mixed-capacity nodegroup (spot + on-demand). node got the preemption notice and then CA immediately started replacing capacity with a new on-demand node. kubelet drain window was too short and caller requests dropped.
Alex: that matches a pattern i've seen: CA will evict/terminate before our drain hooks complete if the node group is marked deletable. We should make spot nodes self-protect during drain by tainting them and extending grace with an on-terminate lifecycle hook.
Riley: +1. Also we need a reliable way to detect the cloud "preemptible" notice and flip node to Unschedulable quickly. currently detection is ~10-20s and sometimes races with autoscaler.
node-drain-bot: :rotating_light: termination-notice for i-0abcd1234 received (GCE SPOT). notice_ttl=120s. current_state=preempting.
Sam: idea: when termination notice arrives, run a small callback that:
- annotate node with `preempting=true`
- add taint `preempting=true:NoSchedule` so new pods don't land there
- call `kubectl drain --force --grace-period=120` and extend app-level shutdown hook via sidecar signal

Example commands:
```
kubectl annotate node ip-10-0-1-23 preempting=true
kubectl taint nodes ip-10-0-1-23 preempting=true:NoSchedule
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-1-23
kubectl drain ip-10-0-1-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```

Priya: we should also teach our pod specs to tolerate but prefer fallback instead of re-queueing to the same spot class. eg add tolerationSeconds so short-lived pods get migrated before they die:
```
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "capacity-type"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "spot"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
    tolerationSeconds: 300
```

Alex: Beyond per-node hooks, CA config needs to prefer draining spot nodes gracefully: set node group priorities and scale-down delays for spot groups. For cluster-autoscaler we use expander:least-waste and `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` but maybe bump `--max-empty-bulk-delete=0` to avoid mass deletes during preempt storms.
Riley: We should also add a short-lived admission webhook that patches pods that are not tolerant-aware (so they don't get stuck) — or better: an init container that registers a lifecycle handler to extend app shutdown (grace-period handshake).
Sam: Outbound plan:
- add detection hook (cloud metadata + instance termination webhook) -> node annotation + taint (1d)
- extend drain grace to 2m, and ensure apps respect SIGTERM handshake via sidecar (2d)
- adjust CA flags for spot nodegroups: longer unneeded-time and priority weights (3d)
- add a small runbook for ops to manually `kubectl cordon && drain` when notices are noisy

Priya: also let's avoid letting CA create new pods on spot nodes while they're draining by labeling nodes with `capacity-type=spot` and changing reprovision controller to prefer `capacity-type=ondemand` as fallback. that way replacement happens in a different group instead of racing.

Alex: one more concrete config snippet for node-template labels for mixed groups in our infra repo:
```
nodeGroup:
  labels:
    capacity-type: spot
  taints:
    - key: "capacity-type"
      value: "spot"
      effect: "PreferNoSchedule"
```

Riley: test plan: simulate termination notices in staging (node-drain-bot can fire synthetic events) and measure 95p request completion rate during scale-down. goal: <1% failed requests during drain.

node-drain-bot: simulated termination injected on staging nodes ip-10-1-*. running drain script. logs: `drain start -> annotate -> taint -> cordon -> graceful drain (120s)`

Priya: great. i'll open a PR with the detection hook + runbook and a CA flag tweak. tagging @Alex for review on node-template changes. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
